newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted sideways in quiet trading at midday on Tuesday in reaction to no physical trades on Monday, traders said.
"The market is very quiet. People are just waiting for more physical trading to set the direction," one broker said.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.70/$25.90 per barrel, largely unchanged from Monday, brokers said.
Brokers said the market is taking a breather from Monday's hectic trading as players locked in earlier physical trades and took positions following news of a fire at the Dumai refinery.
Trading also rose on short covering by one U.S. trader, they said.
"There's not much going on this morning compared to yesterday," another broker said.

The fire at the 125,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Dumai refinery was less serious than originally anticipated and sources close to the refinery said the only damage was due to a 27,500-bpd hyrdrocracker which might be shut down until late April.
The physical market remained firm as bids were still heard at $27.20 per barrel with sellers at 10 cents above the buying number with no trades concluded.
Unlike on Friday when a record 1.91 million barrels were traded as two local traders and one Japanese trader extended their buying spree to more than 13 million barrels.
Fuel oil swaps edged down despite firmer over night crude values on some selling presure with May last quoted at $95.25/$96.25 per tonne, down about 25 cents from Monday, brokers said.
Overnight May Brent closed up 29 cents to $18.17 per barrel, off an intra-day high of $18.30 on the International Petroleum Exchange.
